goal:
Revise your earlier work for the qa phase. The Board rejected it with this comment: QA phase rejected only to unblock the verify step. The application is accepted as built.
QA (ticket 500) may edit tests/test_acceptance.py in this round for exactly these changes:
1. test_AC_52 and test_AC_59: make the hover tests deterministic. Wait for the hover target (element visible and stable), move the mouse, wait for the tooltip. No retries, no skips, no xfail.
2. test_AC_42: keep the 5.0 s limit. Only fix how it measures (one cold start, nothing else running). Do not loosen the number.
Everything else in that file stays unchanged.
Engineer (ticket 501): only act if a test still fails after QA's change. Do not touch tests.
Handover: both agents must end with the handover JSON, and the Tech Lead must store the verify output_tail so failures are visible.
Do not run the full suite more than once per ticket.

acceptance_criteria.text: One test per acceptance item, named after its id

decisions.what: Added target.wait_for(state='visible') to _hover, keeping the existing box-stability wait, then move and wait for tooltip
decisions.why: Board gate 194: deterministic hover (visible, stable, move, wait for tooltip), no retries/skips/xfail; both AC_52 and AC_59 use this helper

decisions.what: AC_42: gc.collect() before and after building each cold client, previous client/response dropped; 5.0 s limit unchanged
decisions.why: Garbage from the previous 200,000-row load or earlier tests must not fall inside the timed cold request
decisions.evidence: tests/test_acceptance.py:1077-1088; python3 -m pytest -s -k AC_42: 2.15 s and 3.61 s

decisions.what: Did not run the full suite or the Playwright browser sweep
decisions.why: Board scoped this round to three test edits; the orchestrator runs check.py qa (full suite) itself and one full run per ticket is the limit

tried_and_failed.what: Reproduce the hover flake under CPU load (32 busy loops on 16 cores)
tried_and_failed.why_it_failed: AC_52 and AC_59 passed under load and alone, so the flake's cause is unconfirmed

assumptions: The flake is load-related timing in the hover step; no hit-test was added because overlapping map points could make an elementFromPoint check hang
The AC_42 gc change is enough; if the full-suite run still exceeds 5.0 s, the timing is machine load from the earlier tests, to be reported as measured
open_questions: If test_AC_52 or test_AC_59 fail again in the orchestrator's full run, I could not confirm the cause. Please store the verify output_tail so the failing step is visible.
test_AC_42 page route (/datasets/{id}) measures about 3.6 s against the 5.0 s limit, the least margin of the two routes.

lessons.lesson: Do not loosen a timing limit to fix a flaky speed test: collect garbage before the timer and keep one cold start per route, then report the measured numbers.
lessons.when: A QA ticket asks to fix how a time-bound acceptance test measures
